stages.name: Requirements
stages.entryQuestion: Before designing a URL shortener, what scope and scale assumptions would you clarify?
stages.objective: Agree on product behavior, measurable quality targets and the stated exercise workload.

completionCriteria.name: Functional scope
completionCriteria.guidance: Distinguish creation, redirects, aliases and expiration; analytics is not required on the redirect critical path.

completionCriteria.name: Quality targets
completionCriteria.guidance: Discuss redirect latency, durable acknowledged writes and the allowed delay for expiration or deletion.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity estimates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use the fictional baseline or state a justified alternative; derive average and peak rates and distinguish payload bytes from replication and indexes.

stages.name: High Level Design
stages.entryQuestion: Walk me through a request from creating a short link to following it.
stages.objective: Separate the write path, redirect lookup and optional analytics path.

completionCriteria.name: Request paths
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain how a client reaches a stateless API or equivalent routing layer.

completionCriteria.name: Mapping ownership
completionCriteria.guidance: Assign code creation, uniqueness and redirect lookup to clear logical responsibilities; separate processes are not required.

completionCriteria.name: Read acceleration
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain when a cache helps and how misses reach the source of truth; Redis is one option.

completionCriteria.name: Click analytics
completionCriteria.guidance: Decouple analytics from redirects if included.

stages.name: Core Flow
stages.entryQuestion: How will you generate short codes and handle collisions or concurrent custom aliases?
stages.objective: Choose one defensible code strategy and preserve unique mappings.

completionCriteria.name: Code strategy
concepts: Random code or unique ID allocation
Base62 as an encoding, not encryption
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose random codes with collision retries or unique IDs plus encoding; do not require both.

completionCriteria.name: Atomic uniqueness
completionCriteria.guidance: Use a unique constraint or equivalent conditional insert so racing writers cannot overwrite an existing alias.

completionCriteria.name: Redirect semantics
completionCriteria.guidance: Define not-found and expired outcomes, and justify 301 versus 302 and cache behavior.

stages.name: Data Model
stages.entryQuestion: What mapping schema and indexes support creation, lookup and expiry?
stages.objective: Model a durable mapping and its access paths.

completionCriteria.name: Mapping schema
completionCriteria.guidance: Include short code, target URL, creation time, expiry and optional owner; avoid storing long URLs in a fixed tiny field.

completionCriteria.name: Lookup indexes
completionCriteria.guidance: Make code lookup and alias uniqueness efficient; choose SQL or key-value storage with justification.

completionCriteria.name: Lifecycle records
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain deletion or tombstones and cleanup without breaking authoritative expiry checks.

stages.name: Reliability
stages.entryQuestion: What happens on a cache miss, cache outage or deletion of a cached link?
stages.objective: Keep redirects correct through cache and storage failures.

completionCriteria.name: Cache lifecycle
completionCriteria.guidance: Bound staleness with expiry-aligned TTLs or invalidation; do not let cache entries outlive an expired link.

completionCriteria.name: Failure behavior
completionCriteria.guidance: Handle cache misses and cache failure without overwhelming the database; define a timeout and degraded behavior.

completionCriteria.name: Durable creation
completionCriteria.guidance: Acknowledge only after the authoritative store accepts the mapping; cover retry idempotency and restore.

stages.name: Scaling
stages.entryQuestion: How would the stated peak redirect and creation load change your partitioning and cache strategy?
stages.objective: Scale the specified workload rather than assuming billions of daily requests.

completionCriteria.name: Partitioning
completionCriteria.guidance: Partition by code or its hash while preserving uniqueness; explain allocation ownership if using IDs.

completionCriteria.name: Hot links
completionCriteria.guidance: Replicate or cache popular immutable mappings; explain stampede protection and controlled negative caching.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity budget
completionCriteria.guidance: Derive 1157.41 average redirects/s and 5787.04 peak redirects/s, plus approximately 182.5 GB of one-year raw mapping data.

stages.name: Tradeoffs
stages.entryQuestion: Which tradeoffs would you make for code allocation, redirect caching and availability?
stages.objective: Defend the choices and their failure semantics.

completionCriteria.name: Allocation tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare one chosen allocation strategy with a credible alternative, including predictability and collisions.

completionCriteria.name: Freshness tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain how permanent HTTP/CDN caching can conflict with deletion or edits; disabling CDN caching is acceptable.

completionCriteria.name: Operational tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Prioritize durable creation and predictable redirects, and identify useful latency, error and cache-hit metrics.
